summary: On-chip flux memory stores persistent currents in superconducting loops to flux-bias circuits such as qubits, and three cell types are built and compared. Once a cell is set, the room-temperature DC sources can be switched off, and a transmon biased this way held its target frequency for 20 hours.
motivation: Every flux-biased device normally needs its own always-on DC line, so wiring and control-source counts grow quickly with system size.
method: Three flux-memory designs are characterized with an in-situ flux detector, then used to bias a transmon, and a two-dimensional multiplexed addressing scheme is proposed.
result: Flux remains in place with the bench sources powered off, the transmon frequency was stable for 20 hours, and the 2D layout would address $N^2$ devices with $2N$ control lines.
